conditions.description: verifyWebhook computes the HMAC over JSON.stringify(req.body) rather than the original request bytes, so parse/reserialize changes can reject legitimately signed payloads.
conditions.rationale: Webhook signatures are normally byte-sensitive; the supplied verifier has discarded the raw byte representation before computing the digest.

conditions.description: crypto.timingSafeEqual throws when the compared buffers have different lengths, and the untrusted signature header length is not checked before the call.
conditions.rationale: A malformed header can turn signature verification into an exception path instead of a clean false result.

conditions.description: The verifier uses crypto.timingSafeEqual rather than ordinary string equality; this is a negative control against inventing a naive comparison defect.
conditions.rationale: Constant-time comparison is explicitly present for equal-length buffers.

conditions.description: Whether deployment middleware also retains a raw request-body buffer elsewhere cannot be established from this fixture.
conditions.rationale: Middleware/runtime configuration is not included in the supplied source.

conditions.description: Webhook verification readiness must not be cleared while raw-byte binding and malformed-signature handling are unresolved or deployment body handling remains unverified.
conditions.rationale: Using HMAC and timingSafeEqual alone is not sufficient evidence that the verification boundary is robust.
